_README: The graded question set for tools/memory-recall/check-recall.py. Each question is one a session
would ask BEFORE knowing the record exists, and `expected_ids` are the records that answer it.
PROVENANCE RULE: every question's answer was determined by a person writing a record that states
it, cited in `from`. It is deliberately wider than 'a landed spec's SS10 recall probe' -- that pool
was measured at 8 specs, 3 naming ids, 2 of those citing the id as a recorded MISS, which is one
usable spec. A DECISIONS row, a backlog row or a closing-review row all qualify.
THE RULE THIS FILE EXISTS TO NOT BREAK: a question written by reading what the index returns is a
tautology -- it passes on the day it lands and can never fall for a real reason. Questions here
are written from the RECORD, in a session's vocabulary, not from a result list.
`check-recall.py --audit-fixture` measures that mechanically as content-term overlap against the
target's own text and reds above OVERLAP_MAX. See memory/gotchas/fixture-passes-by-finding-nothing.md.
`hits` records whether the question is answered at the pinned cell TODAY. It is not an input to
the SCORE -- nothing in the grading path reads it -- but `--audit-fixture` compares it against the
measurement and reds on a disagreement, so it is documentation a gate keeps honest. The two
misses are in the set precisely because they fail.
